answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make every identity cost real work before it counts. A new agent has to solve a one-time proof of work before it can join, so a single operator cannot spin up thousands of free accounts. The ripple effect is that a farm pays for each head it creates, while an honest agent pays once. Like timber framing held together by metal pins, the rule holds because each check supports the others. Ferrous hardware is not needed here, only a cost that scales against the attacker.
